evidence.curator_note: Book draws 4 arc(s); moves <1,2,3,4> are all drawn, and no implicit hook is needed for electron balance. ARC GEOMETRY AS READ FROM THE SCAN (zoomed): the arcs form a bow-tie. Two arcs leave the Si-O sigma bond of the (CH3)3Si-O group (their common tail sits on that bond, mid-way between 'Si' and 'O') and two leave the O(+)-CH2 bond (common tail mid-way between the '+O' and the 'CH2'). Their heads converge in PAIRS: the two upper heads meet in the empty space between the (CH3)3Si and the +O=Si(CH3)2 -- the forming Si-O bond -- and the two lower heads meet in the empty space between the O and the CH2 -- the forming O-CH2 bond. Two heads meeting on one new bond can only be single-electron (fishhook) arcs, so each breaking bond is drawn as contributing one electron to each new bond; that is exactly how the four moves are encoded (electron_count 1 each). The barbs are too coarse in the scan to confirm half-heads by eye, but the 2-heads-per-new-bond geometry settles the count: four full 2-electron arrows would put eight electrons into two new bonds. GENERIC SCHEME INSTANTIATED (convention F): the book writes the chain as -(CH2)n- and the product ring generically; n = 1 was chosen here, i.e. the [M-CH3]+ ion of ethane-1,2-diol bis(TMS) ether, so the neutral is oxirane. Nothing about the electron flow depends on n.

NO MØD RULE IS CROSS-LINKED, and this was CHECKED, not assumed (convention E). rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no '8.117' key at all -- its chapter-8 index runs 8.1-8.14 only (German-edition numbering), so nothing in src/data_generation/rules/ is authored for this equation. Silicon does not occur in ANY rule pattern in the set (a search of every DFS string in rule_index.json['entries'] for 'Si' returns nothing), so no rule can match a silyl-migration substrate at all -- this is a verified gap, not an untested guess.

Status 'inferred', detected=false, no relative_intensity. The precursor m/z in ms_context (191.0919) likewise derives from the n = 1 instantiation, not from the page.
